title: Workers Who Fear AI May be More Prone to Slacking Off - Nautilus
gist: AI companies have shifted from promising to wipe out entire job classes to downplaying a 'jobs apocalypse' amid bipartisan backlash to AI data centers, while the piece argues that fear of AI makes workers more prone to slacking off.

insights.claim: AI company leaders once used the threat of eliminating whole industries as a promotional strategy, such as Sam Altman saying in 2019 that entire classes of jobs will go away and not come back.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: Past rhetoric now creates reputational and political exposure for AI vendors.
insights.quote: Entire classes of jobs will go away and not come back,

insights.claim: Public backlash to AI data centers has reached a fever pitch and is bipartisan, prompting tech leaders to back away from 'jobs apocalypse' claims and promise less disruptive AI.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: Data center siting and permitting risk is rising politically, so watch for softer AI-labor messaging.
insights.locator: Now, with public backlash to AI data centers

insights.claim: The article's framing is that, jobs apocalypse or not, AI job threats have consequences, with workers who fear AI more prone to slacking off.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: Perceived AI displacement may reduce worker productivity; the excerpt does not give the study data.
